messages.content:
You are checking a research plan against a list of experimental controls. You are not asked whether the plan is good. For each control of the list you give two separate answers: CONTENT (does the plan state this control?) and PLACE (is the passage written under an experiment that it can check?).

PLAN. A sequence of actions written one after the other by a planner. Each action adds or revises one proposed experiment and usually has the fields ACTION, TITLE, PROPOSAL, CONTROLS, COST and PREDICTION. Actions are separated by blank lines and are given in the order they were written. Every action counts, including an action that revises an earlier one and an action that looks incomplete.

REFERENCE CONTROLS. A list of experimental controls. Each has an identifier and a description.

CONTENT. Give exactly one content status for each reference control. Judge the content only, wherever the passage is written in the plan.
- "conforme": a passage of the plan states what the description requires (what is compared, held fixed, varied, repeated, measured or excluded). Different wording is fine. Nothing essential is missing or weakened.
- "altere": a passage of the plan states a recognisable but partial, vaguer, reduced or modified version of the control.
- "absent": no passage of the plan states this control.
If the control is stated in several places, keep the best content status found (conforme, then altere, then absent) and quote the passage that earns it. If several passages earn the same best status, quote one whose PLACE is "checks" if there is one.

PLACE. Only for "conforme" and "altere". Read the action that contains your quote, and judge it against the experiment that this action proposes (its TITLE and PROPOSAL), not against the description of the reference control. If that action has no TITLE and no PROPOSAL, answer "general" if the quoted control is general, otherwise "cannot_check".
- "checks": this experiment is one whose result the quoted control would check.
- "cannot_check": this experiment has nothing for the quoted control to compare, hold fixed, vary, repeat, measure or exclude.
- "general": the quoted control names no model, dataset, metric, quantity, condition or comparison that belongs to one experiment; it would apply to any experiment of the plan.
For "absent", PLACE is null. Your PLACE answer must never change your CONTENT answer.

Rules.
1. Judge each reference control on its own. One passage may support several controls.
2. Judge only what is written. Do not credit a control because it would be sensible, usual or implied. Do not lower a status for style, length, order or cost.
3. Evidence. For "conforme" and "altere", quote the passage that carries the control. Copy it character for character from a single action: no ellipsis, no added or removed word, no corrected spelling, no changed punctuation, no paraphrase. Take the shortest passage that is enough: at least 24 characters, at most 300 characters; if the whole field that carries the control is shorter than 24 characters, quote the whole field. A program searches the plan for your quote, word for word; a quote that is not found counts as "absent".
4. For "absent", the quote is null.
5. Give an answer for every reference control, and for no other identifier.

Answer with one JSON object and nothing else, in this form:
{"<identifier>": {"content": "conforme" | "altere" | "absent", "quote": "<quote>" | null, "place": "checks" | "cannot_check" | "general" | null}, ...}

PLAN
<<<
ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of replacing the system prompt with a neutral one on agreement with the reference labels for Brindle-XL
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Brindle-XL on the Kettering proofs and measure agreement with the reference labels before and after replacing the system prompt with a neutral one.
CONTROLS: (1) Repeat the evaluation of agreement with the reference labels on the Kettering proofs with a second prompt template.
COST: 13 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Agreement with the reference labels improves by a small but reliable margin on the Kettering proofs.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of halving the learning rate on exact-match accuracy for Quillon-L
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Quillon-L on the Brenna-QA set and measure exact-match accuracy before and after halving the learning rate.
CONTROLS: (1) Report edit distance to the reference on the Brenna-QA set to check that the gain is not an artifact of one metric.
COST: 29 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Exact-match accuracy improves by a small but reliable margin on the Brenna-QA set.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of ablating the retrieval head on false-alarm rate at fixed recall for Ilexa-6
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Ilexa-6 on the Wexcombe caption set and measure false-alarm rate at fixed recall before and after ablating the retrieval head.
CONTROLS: (1) Run Ilexa-6 on the Wexcombe caption set with five random seeds and report the spread of false-alarm rate at fixed recall.
COST: 2 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: False-alarm rate at fixed recall degrades on the Osric code suite while it holds on the Wexcombe caption set.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of masking named entities on pass rate on hidden tests for Halden-S
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Halden-S on the Halvard corpus and measure pass rate on hidden tests before and after masking named entities.
CONTROLS: (1) Run Halden-S on the Halvard corpus with five random seeds and report the spread of pass rate on hidden tests.
COST: 35 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Pass rate on hidden tests degrades on the Pryce reasoning chains while it holds on the Halvard corpus.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of removing the warm-up phase on refusal rate for Ostrava-7
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Ostrava-7 on the Tolwyn dialogue logs and measure refusal rate before and after removing the warm-up phase.
CONTROLS: (1) Evaluate on the Senna safety prompts as a held-out distribution.
COST: 16 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: No change in refusal rate beyond seed noise on the Tolwyn dialogue logs.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of replacing the system prompt with a neutral one on agreement with the reference labels for Brindle-XL
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Brindle-XL on the Kettering proofs and measure agreement with the reference labels before and after replacing the system prompt with a neutral one.
CONTROLS: (1) Include Sundrow-M as a baseline under the same training budget.
COST: 36 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Agreement with the reference labels improves by a small but reliable margin on the Kettering proofs.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of halving the learning rate on exact-match accuracy for Quillon-L
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Quillon-L on the Brenna-QA set and measure exact-match accuracy before and after halving the learning rate.
CONTROLS: (1) Report edit distance to the reference on the Brenna-QA set to check that the gain is not an artifact of one metric.
COST: 35 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Exact-match accuracy improves by a small but reliable margin on the Brenna-QA set.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of ablating the retrieval head on false-alarm rate at fixed recall for Ilexa-6
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Ilexa-6 on the Wexcombe caption set and measure false-alarm rate at fixed recall before and after ablating the retrieval head.
CONTROLS: (1) Match the number of training steps between Ilexa-6 and Varnok-2B.
COST: 32 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: No change in false-alarm rate at fixed recall beyond seed noise on the Wexcombe caption set.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of masking named entities on pass rate on hidden tests for Halden-S
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Halden-S on the Halvard corpus and measure pass rate on hidden tests before and after masking named entities.
CONTROLS: (1) Evaluate on the Pryce reasoning chains as a held-out distribution.
COST: 4 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Pass rate on hidden tests degrades on the Pryce reasoning chains while it holds on the Halvard corpus.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of removing the warm-up phase on refusal rate for Ostrava-7
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Ostrava-7 on the Tolwyn dialogue logs and measure refusal rate before and after removing the warm-up phase.
CONTROLS: (1) Ablate removing the warm-up phase alone, keeping data and optimizer fixed, to isolate its effect on refusal rate.
COST: 33 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: No change in refusal rate beyond seed noise on the Tolwyn dialogue logs.
>>>

REFERENCE CONTROLS
- id: c1 | description: Repeat the run of Halden-S on the Halvard corpus over several random seeds and report the variation of pass rate on hidden tests.
- id: c2 | description: Isolate the effect of removing the warm-up phase on refusal rate by changing it alone, with data and optimizer held fixed.
- id: c3 | description: Evaluate on the Senna safety prompts, a distribution that was not used for training.
- id: c4 | description: Measure mean token overlap on the Lowick tabular benchmark again with a different prompt template.
- id: c5 | description: Compare against Corvane-12 as a baseline trained with an identical budget.
- id: c6 | description: Use the Lowick tabular benchmark with shuffled labels as a negative control for mean token overlap.
